high.title: VN-Index "Well-Positioned" to Break 1,800 Points — Securities Firms Highlight Stocks with Unique Catalysts and Attractive Valuations
high.summary:
Vietnam's equity market endured a turbulent July 2026, with liquidity remaining at depressed levels reflecting broad investor caution and a "wait-and-see" posture across institutional and retail money. The securities, real estate, banking, and technology sectors bore the brunt of the correction. The VN-Index found near-term support around the 1,651-point level.

Entering August, Agriseco Research forecasts a recovery rally targeting the 1,800-point zone. Key catalysts cited include: (1) government stimulus measures and accelerated public investment disbursement, (2) continued FDI attraction policies, and (3) compelling valuations — the market currently trades at approximately 11.7x P/E, below its 5-year historical average.

**Key risks to the upside scenario** include inflationary pressures, persistent net foreign selling, and global geopolitical uncertainty. For international fund managers, the combination of low valuations and upcoming FTSE upgrade-related inflows (see Article 4) creates a potentially constructive setup, though the continued net foreign outflow trend warrants close monitoring before increasing equity exposure.

high.title: Billions of USD Poised to Flow into Vietnamese Equities — Range of Stocks Forecast to Attract Heavy Capital Inflows
high.summary:
This is a highly market-moving development for foreign capital flows into Vietnam. On **21 August 2026**, FTSE Russell is scheduled to officially announce the constituent stocks to be included in the **FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS)** Emerging Markets index, effective **21 September 2026**. This marks Vietnam's formal entry into the FTSE EM upgrade pathway — a milestone years in the making.

**Estimated capital inflows:**
- FTSE estimates total inflows of approximately **USD 6 billion** from both active and passive funds post-upgrade.
- ETFs tracking FTSE indices alone are projected to deploy approximately **USD 1.5 billion** over a 12-month rollout period.
- In the base case, MB Securities (MBS) estimates **~USD 150 million** from ETFs will be deployed in the **September 2026 rebalancing**, concentrated in large-cap names.
- MBS forecasts approximately **30 stocks** will be included in FTSE GEIS, with **VIC (Vingroup)** projected as the largest beneficiary at ~USD 46.4 million in net buying, representing ~1.19% of its market cap.

**FX and bond market implications:** A USD 6 billion inflow pipeline — even if phased — represents a material positive for VND stability and could provide the SBV with room to rebuild foreign reserves. Fund managers should front-run the September rebalancing date and monitor the 21 August FTSE announcement closely as a near-term catalyst.

high.title: BIDV Bank's Latest Deposit Interest Rates for August 2026
high.summary: BIDV, one of Vietnam's four largest state-owned commercial banks, has published its official deposit rate schedule for August 2026. Key rate levels are as follows: short-term deposits (1–5 months) are capped at **4.75%/year**, in compliance with the SBV's regulatory ceiling on sub-6-month deposits. Medium-term deposits (6–11 months) are set at **6.6%/year**, while all long-term tenors from 12 to 36 months are uniformly priced at **6.8%/year** — the highest offered rate in BIDV's online schedule. Online deposits continue to offer marginally better rates than over-the-counter placements. USD deposits remain at **0%/year**, reinforcing Vietnam's ongoing de-dollarization policy.

high.title: Five Major Vietnamese Banks Now Earn Over VND 10,000 Billion Per Quarter — Vietcombank Posts Record VND 17,420 Billion in Q2/2026
high.summary: Vietnam's banking sector has reached a new profitability threshold, with five major banks — Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV, MB, and VPBank — each reporting pre-tax profits exceeding VND 10,000 billion in Q2/2026 alone. Vietcombank led the pack with a record quarterly profit of VND 17,420 billion, up nearly 58% year-on-year and the highest quarterly result in the bank's history. Less than a decade ago, VND 10,000 billion was considered an ambitious full-year target for most Vietnamese banks.

high.title: In Exactly 15 Days, Vietnam's Stock Market Awaits a Major Announcement
high.summary:
On August 21, 2026 — just 15 days away — FTSE Russell will officially publish the list of Vietnamese stocks to be included in the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS) under its Emerging Market classification. The full upgrade takes effect September 21, 2026, at which point all Vietnamese equities will simultaneously be removed from the FTSE Frontier Index Series.

This is a landmark capital flow event for Vietnam. Analysis from Vietcap highlights that the upgrade was triggered by Vietnam meeting key market accessibility criteria, most critically the implementation of the **Global Broker model**, enabling foreign institutional investors to trade via global brokerages as counterparties. This was underpinned by **Circular 08/2026/TT-BTC** and improvements to the **Non Pre-Funding (NPF)** mechanism — long a structural barrier to foreign participation.

medium.title: Over 6,400 Staff Exit Reports of 8 Banks — Top 14 Companies Cut Combined 21,730 Employees in H1 2026
medium.summary:
Financial statements from the 14 largest workforce-reducing companies in H1 2026 reveal a combined headcount reduction of 21,730 employees, reflecting broad-based labor restructuring across the Vietnamese economy. The largest absolute reduction was at FPT Group (-9,722 staff), primarily attributable to a structural reorganization in which FPT Telecom (~10,000 employees) was transferred under the Ministry of Public Security's ownership oversight from July 2025 — not a genuine business contraction. More relevant to banking sector watchers, **8 banks collectively shed over 6,400 staff**, with **Sacombank (STB)** recording the steepest percentage decline among listed firms. For bond and equity investors, banking sector headcount reductions can signal cost rationalization efforts — potentially supportive of near-term profitability metrics — but also raise questions about credit underwriting capacity and loan growth momentum in H2 2026. Worth monitoring in upcoming Q2 2026 bank earnings releases.

---

medium.title: HDBank Plans Total 30% Dividend and Bonus Share Issuance
medium.summary: HDBank (HDB) is seeking shareholder approval for a combined 30% capital increase — comprising a 25% stock dividend from 2025 retained earnings (up to ~1.25 billion new shares) and an additional 5% bonus issue from the charter capital reserve fund (~250 million shares). The shareholder voting window runs August 3–14, 2026, with eligibility based on the July 28 record date. While this is primarily a corporate action, the significant dilution and capital base expansion of a mid-tier listed bank has implications for the broader banking sector equity valuations and could influence the VN-Index weighting of financial stocks. Investors should monitor execution risk and the secondary market impact on HDB share price post-issuance.

medium.title: A Bank Set to Pay 15% Stock Dividend — MB Bank
medium.summary: MB Bank (MBB), a major listed commercial bank on HoSE, has announced August 12, 2026 as the record date for a **15% stock dividend**, involving the issuance of over 1.2 billion new shares (~VND 12,082.5 billion at par value) funded from 2025 undistributed profits. Simultaneously, MB will conduct a rights offering of ~805.5 million shares at a 10:1 ratio (shareholders receive the right to purchase 1 new share per 10 held), registered under SSC certificate No. 335/GCN-UBCK dated July 31, 2026. The combined capital raising effort signals continued balance sheet expansion among major Vietnamese banks, which is relevant for equity investors tracking banking sector weight on the VN-Index, as well as for assessing sector-wide credit growth and capital adequacy dynamics.

medium.title: Agribank August 2026 Deposit Rates Unchanged — Peak Rate Holds at 6% per Annum
medium.summary: State-owned Agribank has held its deposit rate schedule unchanged into August 2026, maintaining a dual-rate structure for counter (branch) and online savings products. Counter rates range from 0.2% p.a. (demand deposits) up to a peak of **6.0% p.a. for 24-month tenors**. Key benchmark tenors: 6–11 months at 4.0% p.a.; 12–18 months at 5.9% p.a. Online savings rates are slightly higher than counter rates across equivalent tenors. The stability of Agribank's rates — as the largest state-owned bank by assets — signals that the SBV is comfortable with the current monetary policy stance and sees no immediate need to adjust the deposit rate ceiling. For bond investors, the 12–18 month deposit rate corridor of ~5.9% remains an important anchor for short-to-medium tenor government bond yield expectations. No imminent rate cut signals are evident from this data.

medium.title: Vietcap Names 29 Stocks Likely to Receive Billion-Dollar Inflows Post-Upgrade
medium.summary: Vietcap Securities has published a forecast list of 29 Vietnamese stocks it expects to qualify for inclusion in the FTSE GEIS emerging markets index, meaningfully exceeding FTSE Russell's own preliminary list of 23 stocks published earlier. The discrepancy arises because Vietcap's analysis uses data updated to June 30, 2026, whereas FTSE Russell's reference list was based on December 31, 2025 data — a six-month gap during which stock prices, free-float ratios, foreign ownership room, liquidity, and investable market capitalisation have shifted substantially. The report identifies four large-cap stocks within the 29-name universe. For EM portfolio managers, this analysis is actionable: the gap between Vietcap's 29-stock forecast and FTSE Russell's 23-stock preliminary list represents potential upside surprise in inclusion breadth. Broader inclusion means larger aggregate passive inflows and wider dispersion of capital across the Vietnamese equity market. FX traders should note that confirmation of a larger inclusion universe on August 21 could meaningfully support VND through anticipated USD inflows from global index funds ahead of the September 21 effective date.

medium.title: China Announces 20% Tax on Offshore Trust Assets — Ultra-Wealthy Scramble to Comply
medium.summary: China's Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration issued on July 24 their most comprehensive regulations to date on taxing assets held through offshore trusts, imposing a 20% tax rate covering the full lifecycle of a trust — from establishment, income generation, and profit distribution through to termination. Critically, individuals must declare and settle outstanding tax liabilities on assets transferred into offshore trusts since the start of 2023, with only a 90-day window (deadline: October 22) before penalties and late interest accrue. Wealthy Chinese families based in Hong Kong and Singapore are reportedly rushing to engage legal counsel, assess liabilities, and in some cases liquidate assets to meet the deadline. While not a Vietnam-specific story, this development carries indirect relevance for Vietnamese capital markets: asset reallocation by Chinese HNW individuals and family offices under tax pressure could redirect capital flows across Southeast Asian markets, including Vietnam. Additionally, any acceleration of Chinese capital flight or structural shifts in regional wealth management could influence USD liquidity dynamics in ASEAN FX markets, worth monitoring for second-order VND effects.

medium.title: A Major Force Net Sells Over VND 700 Billion in HOSE Shares — Foreigners Remain Net Buyers
medium.summary: In the August 5 session, the VN-Index edged down a marginal 0.77 points (-0.04%) to close at 1,776.46 points, reflecting mild corrective pressure. Securities companies' proprietary trading desks (tự doanh) were net sellers of VND 728 billion on HOSE, with the heaviest selling concentrated in GEE (VND 285 billion), GAS (VND 77 billion), VPB (VND 51 billion), and VCB (VND 50 billion). In contrast, foreign investors maintained a constructive stance, net buying VND 478 billion across the entire market. The divergence between domestic institutional selling and foreign net inflows is a key dynamic worth tracking — sustained foreign net buying provides a marginal positive for VND via equity-related USD conversion demand, while broker proprietary desk selling may reflect short-term profit-taking rather than a fundamental shift in outlook.

medium.title: Vietcombank Books VND 2,900 Billion Gain Following Full Acquisition of Prime 35-Story Tower in Ho Chi Minh City
medium.summary: Vietcombank has completed the acquisition of a 100% stake in Vietcombank-Bonday-Benthanh LLC, the entity owning the 35-floor Vietcombank Tower at 5 Me Linh Square, Ho Chi Minh City. The bank previously held 52% and acquired the remaining 48% (18% from Setra, 30% from Bonday) at a total implied enterprise valuation of approximately VND 6,679 billion. Under business combination accounting rules, the pre-existing 52% stake — previously carried on books at VND 564 billion — was remeasured to fair value upon obtaining control, generating a one-off fair value gain of approximately VND 2,906 billion in Q2/2026 other income. While this is a non-recurring accounting gain, it partially inflates headline profits and NIMs for the quarter. Bond and equity investors should note this item when normalizing Vietcombank's underlying operating performance for Q2/2026.

medium.title: A Private Bank Expands Its Asset Base More Than the Big 4 Combined — Equal to BIDV and Agribank Together
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking sector showed clear bifurcation in H1 2026, with private banks outpacing state-owned peers in asset growth. **VPBank** led the entire system, growing total assets by VND 242,377 billion (+19.2%) to VND 1.502 quadrillion, surpassing the combined absolute asset growth of Agribank and BIDV. Vietcombank ranked second with an increase of approximately VND 215 trillion. Notably, Sacombank and Eximbank were the only two banks to record asset contraction. Of the 28 banks surveyed, the vast majority grew assets versus end-2025.
